A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimNPO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the substantial reorganization. Specific reporting inconsistencies are addressed below.

before.justification: v1 reports original Markov-chain simulations, TOFU/MUSE/WMDP evaluations, ablations, relearning attacks, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds controlled TOFU memorization, optimization-divergence, and sequential MUSE unlearning results.

M1.justification: The SimNPO objective, length-normalized reference-free reward, default reward margin, gradient weighting, and retain-loss regularization remain unchanged in Equations (1), (4), and (5). The added experiments and explanations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds sequential MUSE News unlearning across four requests, introducing repeated-forgetting task requirements (Appendix 8.4). It removes WMDP cybersecurity coverage and results, retaining biosecurity only. TOFU Forget05/Forget10, MUSE Books/News, and the Markov-chain scenarios otherwise remain.

E2.justification: Retained comparisons preserve their comparator membership: GA, GradDiff, IDK, NPO, and Retrain on TOFU; Task Vector and the existing optimization baselines on MUSE; and RMU/NPO on WMDP-Bio. The weighted-GradDiff comparison is relocated, and new analyses reuse existing methods.

E3.justification: New protocols train the original TOFU model on only half the forget examples before unlearning both halves, track KL distance from the original model during optimization, and evaluate sequential MUSE requests. Existing benchmark training budgets largely remain. The MUSE caption now correctly assigns LLaMA2 to News and ICLM to Books, matching both versions' setup text; this does not establish an actual model switch.

E4.justification: v3 adds a controlled memorization-level analysis, a GA/NPO/SimNPO divergence-speed comparison, and sequential-unlearning robustness evidence. It removes v1's MUSE Min-K% distribution analysis of over-forgetting (Figure 7). The response-length analysis, weighted-GradDiff comparison, hyperparameter heatmaps, Markov-chain studies, and relearning attacks are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 explicitly reports five independent trials for both TOFU forget sizes. After splitting the table, v3 states five trials for Forget05, while Forget10 Table A3 only references the same table format, making its run count less explicit. Five-run relearning averages and variance reporting remain. This is a disclosure change, not evidence of fewer runs.

E6.justification: MUSE News rows change for GradDiff and SimNPO; SimNPO's PrivLeak changes from 11.90 to 72.93 and retain KnowMem from 40.31 to 39.65. The Bio-only WMDP table reports NPO/SimNPO forgetting scores of 0.74/0.74 instead of 0.581/0.584, reversing their ranking against RMU. TOFU Forget10 SimNPO utility changes from 0.63 to 0.62. Memorization, speed, and sequential results are added; cybersecurity, Min-K%, and cost results are removed. Setting/reporting differences limit direct performance comparisons. v3 also misattributes Books PrivLeak -31.17 to SimNPO in prose; its table assigns that value to NPO and retains -19.82 for SimNPO.

T1.justification: The existing gradient derivation and Markov-chain definitions remain. New Appendix 6 introduces simplifying assumptions about normalized log probabilities and reference likelihood, derives approximate optimization dynamics, and estimates length-dependent unlearning steps for NPO versus length-independent steps for SimNPO. This is a substantial new analytical argument, presented heuristically rather than as a general guarantee.

C1.justification: Both versions identify reference-model bias, propose the same SimNPO framework, and claim advantages over NPO supported by benchmark, synthetic, and relearning experiments. The expanded abstract and introduction articulate the existing failure mechanisms more explicitly without changing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 expands the memorization-level explanation and adds interpretations of divergence speed and sequential robustness. For WMDP, v1 hypothesizes weaker effectiveness in capability removal; v3 instead reports stronger forgetting than RMU and explains lower utility through whole-model versus selected-layer updates. It newly acknowledges missing theoretical guarantees and removes the dedicated broader-impacts discussion.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents RMU's updates to layers 5–7 versus whole-model updates for NPO/SimNPO and specifies the controlled memorization experiment's training-set construction. It removes the GPU-memory/runtime table and accompanying efficiency discussion. Hardware, most hyperparameter searches, and the stated code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhang et al.'s defensive-unlearning citation and removes Ji et al.'s forget-retain/logit-difference work and Shi et al.'s pretraining-data detection reference. Consolidating the Kurmanji preprint/publication entries does not remove a distinct work. Positioning relative to NPO, DPO, and SimPO remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, Section 4 is reorganized around explicit examples, and the experimental narrative and conclusion are condensed. Detailed setups and several analyses move into extensively reorganized numbered appendices. These changes substantially alter the narrative and document structure beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a full-width four-panel display with a memorization panel. The length-distribution displays are consolidated and replotted, the TOFU table is split between main text and appendix, and WMDP and weighted-GradDiff displays move to appendices. New speed and sequential plots accompany removal of the Min-K% figure and resource-cost table.

improvement.justification: The controlled TOFU memorization experiment directly strengthens the central reference-bias argument beyond v1's length-based and Markov-chain evidence. Sequential MUSE evaluation and clearer organization also improve the paper. These gains support a limited net improvement: substantial supporting evidence already existed, while v3 removes cybersecurity, privacy-distribution, and resource-cost evidence and introduces a Books PrivLeak prose/table misattribution. Higher revised benchmark scores alone do not establish better quality.
